questions.a: The Levite was living in a remote area of the hill country of Ephraim.

questions.q: Where did the Levite’s concubine bring him?
questions.a: The concubine brought the Levite into the house of her father.

questions.q: Although the Levite intended to go home, what did his father-in-law want him to do?
questions.a: His father-in-law wanted him to stay and spend the night.

questions.q: What did the Levite’s father-in-law ask him to do again on the fifth day?
questions.a: His father-in-law asked him to stay another night and have a good time.

questions.q: Why did the Levite not want to spend the night in Jebus?
questions.a: The Levite did not want to stay in a city where there were no other Israelites.

questions.q: Why did the Levite and his servant sit down in the city square?
questions.a: They sat down in the city square, for no one had offered them a place to stay for the night.

questions.q: From what tribe were the men living in Gibeah?
questions.a: The men living in Gibeah were from the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.q: What did the old man warn the Levite not to do?
questions.a: The old man warned the Levite not to spend the night in the open square.

questions.q: Why did the wicked men of the city want the old man to bring out the man who was staying in his house?
questions.a: The wicked men of the city wanted the old man to bring out the man who came was staying in his house so they could have sex with him.

questions.q: Who did the old man offer to the wicked men in place of the Levite?
questions.a: The old man offered them his virgin daughter and the Levite’s concubine.
At dawn the wicked men let the concubine go. She came and she fell down at the door of the man’s house where her master was, and she lay there until it was light.

questions.q: What did the Levite do when his concubine did not answer him?
questions.a: When the Levite’s concubine did not answer him, he put her body on the donkey and set out for home.

questions.q: What did the Levite do to his concubine’s body?
questions.a: The Levite cut her up into twelve pieces and sent the pieces to each of the tribes throughout Israel.

commentary.text: The wickedness of the men of Gibeah.

—The three remaining chapters of this book contain a very sad history of the wickedness of the men of Gibeah, in Benjamin. The righteous Lord permits sinners to execute just vengeance on one another, and if the scene here described is horrible, what will the discoveries of the day of judgment be! Let each of us consider how to escape from the wrath to come, how to mortify the sins of our own hearts, to resist Satan's temptations, and to avoid the pollutions there are in the world.
